content.comment_body: Hi, In previous threads about the cursor keys, the usual workaround suggested is to hold Escape plus a cursor key. It’s a bit inconvenient but does work, provided you’re on the screen with the cursor indicator. On other screens, the operator device tends to flicker between the menu and the default diagnostic screens. Is there a way to have the escape function work universally, or better yet, make the cursors respond as they do in the programming software? Ideally, it would be great if they behaved like the function keys. If it helps, I’m using a [product_name] with [article_no] and [product_name] operator device. If not possible, I’ll add external controls, but a built-in solution would be appreciated.

I doubt you have a [article_no]. That would typically be a [product_name] version whose article number ends with [article_no]. Starting with [product_name] [version_no], there were changes to the cursor key behavior when using the ESC key. Now, holding ESC together with a cursor key is no longer supported. The reasoning isn’t clear, but it may relate to how key debouncing is handled.

It does say [article_no] on the front—I bought it a couple of months ago from a well-known distributor as something to experiment with. On the correct screen (showing ESC+C and the cursors), ESC+Cursor works; elsewhere it just flickers between the menu and the current screen. As mentioned, I can work around it, but knowing this limitation with the cursors, I probably wouldn’t have chosen this operator device. My plan was to use the arrow keys for workshop light controls before installing sensors. The function keys currently operate my tool cabinet locks and transformers. Still, I’ll likely find creative uses for the screen.

What you’re referencing is the article number, such as [article_no]. The key digits indicate there's a [product_name] [article_no], which is the [product_name] [version_no] series. Delivery is listed as [product_name] [version_no].

Yes, I see [article_no] on the hardware and [article_no] on the operator device, as well as [product_name] [version_no] in the programming software. If the cursor keys are limited in this way, I’ll install external switches. To be honest, I didn’t realize it was the [version_no] version—I just got the starter kit from a distributor as a project during slow work periods and thought building a feature-rich light switch would be an interesting pastime.

analysis.insight_summary: Users report inconsistent navigation when using cursor keys with the ESC key on the [product_name] operator device. The expected behavior, similar to the [product_name] programming software, is missing on some screens, causing interruptions and confusion. Changes implemented in the [version_no] series seem to have altered key functions, restricting ESC+Cursor actions to certain screens and causing display flicker elsewhere.
analysis.user_expectations: Users hope to see the ESC+Cursor key combination work uniformly on all screens of the [product_name] operator device, closely matching the ease of use found in the [product_name] programming software. They’re looking for navigation and physical key controls that are straightforward, reliable, and adaptable for flexible automation.
